Hi Marissa — thanks for the materials and the clear recap. A couple of clarifying questions from our legal and infra teams before we escalate to procurement: 

1) Controller/Processor: We need a clear statement in the DPA that Velaris is the Controller and Redwood is the Processor. Is that already covered in v3?

2) Subprocessors: We need to know which subprocessors will have access to logs/PII (not just category). Can you confirm whether any analytics vendors or managed services have access to raw logs?

3) Breach notification: We typically require notification within 48 hours of discovery. Can Redwood commit to that timeframe, or is 72 hours standard for you?

4) Data residency & Dedicated option: We are targeting AWS us-west-2 for data residency. Can you confirm if Hosted API (hosted.redwood.ai) can guarantee regional isolation, or would we need Dedicated/Private?

5) Retention & logging controls: We need the option to shorten retention of raw logs to 30 days and to disable collecting request/response bodies for specific endpoints (PII-intensive). Is that supported?

If you can loop in Legal + SE with answers, we can get procurement engaged.

Thanks,

Hi all — quick technical answers to the questions below: 

- Controller/Processor: (for clarity) from a technical standpoint we operate as a Processor — we never use customer data to train models beyond the explicit opt-in workflows. Legal can provide the exact clause.

- Subprocessors & log access: Our subprocessors list (attached) includes categories and names. Specifically, managed infra partners (our cloud provider) and a small set of telemetry/monitoring vendors have access to aggregated metrics; only our log-storage subprocessor has access to raw logs. If you want the exact vendor name for the log-storage subprocessor we can provide it under NDA — we usually provide that during procurement.

- Logging controls & retention: We support configurable retention windows. Defaults are 90 days for raw request logs and 365 days for aggregated telemetry. For Dedicated/Private deployments you can set retention to any value (including 30 days) via policy. For Hosted customers we can offer per-account retention settings; for route-level disabling of request/response bodies we have a feature flag that strips bodies before storage (can be enabled per-api-key or per-route).

- Data residency: Hosted API is multi-region but does not offer strict regional isolation on the shared plane. If you require guaranteed residency (data never leaving us-west-2), Dedicated or Private deployment is the recommended path — we can scope a Dedicated plan that pins capacity to us-west-2.

- Encryption & pseudonymization: Data at rest is AES-256 encrypted; in-flight TLS. We also support pseudonymization for tokens/identifiers prior to persistence.

Next steps: I can put together a short tech note (1 page) outlining retention defaults, route-level body stripping, and the subprocessors access model.

Regards,
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 17 Feb 2026 10:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: DPA clarifications & data handling (Velaris Systems)

Hi Samantha — thanks for the detailed questions. A few legal points and proposed language to keep the procurement process moving: 

1) Controller/Processor: Redwood confirms the standard allocation in our DPA: the customer (Velaris Systems) is the Controller; Redwood is the Processor. We will update v3 to add an explicit sentence in Section 1 (Definitions) making that clear.

2) Subprocessors: Our subprocessors list (attached) is our current state. We are willing to provide the specific vendor name for the log-storage subprocessor under an NDA if required by procurement. We will also add a clause to v3 that commits to notifying you 30 days prior to adding a new subprocessor and offering objection rights consistent with industry norms.

3) Breach notification: Our standard is to notify affected customers "without undue delay and within 72 hours of confirming a security incident". We understand your preference for 48 hours. We can propose the following compromise for the DPA: Redwood will notify Velaris of confirmed data incidents within 72 hours; for incidents classified as "material customer data exposure" Redwood will use its best efforts to notify within 48 hours and will provide continuous updates until containment. Let us know if that is acceptable.

4) Retention & logging controls: We can accept a contractual commitment to a 30-day retention for raw logs for Hosted customers where technically feasible or guarantee it for Dedicated deployments. We will add language to the DPA that we will provide route-level body-stripping controls (as described by Rishi) and will cooperate on implementation.

5) Next steps: 
- We will prepare DPA v3.1 with the explicit controller/processor sentence, the subprocessor notice clause, and the breach language above.
- If you are comfortable with v3.1, we will circulate a DocuSign link for signature.

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/VEL-2026-042/dpa

Please let me know if Velaris procurement wants any alternate language; we can escalate to our CISO/legal for negotiation but prefer to keep things within this scope to avoid delays.

Best regards,
Lauren Bishop
Head of Legal, Redwood Inference
